links.outcome: Diagnostic accuracy of AI models versus orthopedic and radiology attending physicians on external validation set
links.effect: Distributed AI accuracy 0.9636 vs centralized 0.9632 (p>0.05), orthopedic physician 0.9291, radiology attending 0.9175 (p<0.05). AI diagnosis time 4.99 min vs about 25-26 min for physicians.
links.quote: In the external validation set, the accuracy reached 0.9636 [95% CI (0.9388, 0.9762)], was slightly higher than that of the centralized YOLOv8n model at 0.9632 [95% CI (0.9387, 0.9755)] (p > 0.05), and exceeded the orthopedic physician at 0.9291 [95% CI (0.9002, 0.9482)] and radiology attending physician at 0.9175 [95% CI (0.8891, 0.9393)], with a statistically significant difference (p < 0.05).

unlisted_practices: Blockchain-based federated learning so training data stays within each hospital
Multi-hospital distributed model training with parameter aggregation

screen.reason: The study evaluates an imaging AI model for tibial plateau fractures, including a reader study comparing standalone physician performance versus AI-assisted attending physicians.
